Let $n=1000$, $m=2017$ and write $A=\{a_1<a_2<\dots<a_n\}$. Split
$$B=A\cap[1,2n],\qquad L=A\cap[2n+1,m],$$
with $|B|=s$, $|L|=r$, so $s+r=n$ and $r\le m-2n=17$. Since $i,j\le n$, we have $i+j\le 2n$; thus only elements of $B$ can trigger the condition $i+j\in A$.

**1. $B\subseteq[1,2s+1]$.** If $i,j>s$ then $i+j\ge2s+2$ while $a_i,a_j\ge2n+1$, so $a_i+a_j>m$, impossible. Hence $B\cap[2s+2,2n]=\varnothing$, i.e. $b_s\le2s+1$.

**2. If $s>k+r-2$ then $B=[1,s]$.** Suppose $B\ne[1,s]$ and set $V=B\cap[s+1,2s+1]$, $t=|V|\ge1$. For $v\in V$ with $v\le2s$, take $i=v-s\le s$, $j=s$; then $i+j=v\in B$ forces $b_{v-s}+b_s\in L$. Since $b_i\ge i$ and $b_s\ge s+t$, this sum is $\ge v+t\ge2n+1=2s+2r+1$, giving $v\ge2s+2r+1-t$. With $v\le2s$ we get $t\ge2r+1$. Distinct $v$ give distinct sums, so $r\ge t$, contradiction.

Thus some $v=2s+1\in V$. Then $i+j=2s+1$ forces exactly one index, say $j$, to exceed $s$; so $j\in[s+1,s+r]$ and $i=2s+1-j\in[s+1-r,s]$. Then
$$a_i+a_j=b_i+\ell_{j-s}\ge(s+1-r)+(2n+1)=2n+s+2-r>m$$
whenever $s>k+r-2$, again a contradiction. Hence $V=\varnothing$ and $B=[1,s]$.

**3. Counting.** Here $r\le17$ and $s=n-r\ge983$, while $k+r-2\le32$, so $s>k+r-2$ always holds. Thus $a_i=i$ for $i\le s$, and the remaining $r$ elements form an arbitrary $r$-subset of $\{2001,2002,\dots,2017\}$. Conversely every such set works, because $i+j\in A$ happens only when $i+j\le s$, and then $a_i+a_j=i+j\in A$.

The number of admissible sets is $\displaystyle\sum_{r=0}^{17}\binom{17}{r}=2^{17}=131072$.
